name: labelled_spss
title: Labelled vector with SPSS user missings

origin.description: A labelled vector that also records SPSS user-defined missing values.
origin.usage: labelled_spss(x = double(), labels = NULL, na_values = NULL, na_range = NULL, label = NULL)

arguments.name: labels
arguments.text: A named vector of the same type.

arguments.name: na_values
arguments.text: Values that count as missing. na_value is the same for a single value.

arguments.name: na_range
arguments.text: An inclusive range of length two, in ascending order.

origin.details: This class is what read_sav returns when user_na is true. is.na includes the discrete values and the range.
origin.example:
x1 <- labelled_spss(1:10, c(Good = 1, Bad = 8), na_values = c(9, 10))
print(is.na(x1))

translation.description: A labelled vector that also records SPSS user-defined missing values.
translation.usage: labelled_spss(x=None, labels=None, na_values=None, na_range=None, label=None, na_value=None)

arguments.name: labels
arguments.text: A named vector of the same type.

arguments.name: na_values
arguments.text: Values that count as missing. na_value is the same for a single value.

arguments.name: na_range
arguments.text: An inclusive range of length two, in ascending order.

translation.details: This class is what read_sav returns when user_na is true. is.na includes the discrete values and the range.
translation.example:
from haven import labelled_spss
from haven.labelled import is_missing
x1 = labelled_spss(list(range(1, 11)), {"Good": 1, "Bad": 8}, na_values=[9, 10])
print(is_missing(x1))
